reason: Both conversations correctly escalate to an engineer without proposing dismantling, but Conversation 1 moved more efficiently with sensible questions (type, zone, child lock) and a genuinely owner-safe pan test, then asked for the full model number before any part could be considered, which matches the expected path. Conversation 2 front-loaded generic child-lock/induction-pan boilerplate, asked the homeowner to visually inspect the coil under a ceramic glass top (impractical, prompting pushback) and referenced a 'simmerstat' that doesn't apply to touch controls, though it did more honestly keep the control/wiring alternative open and advised not using the zone. Conversation 1's final 'failed element' heading is a touch overconfident given the hidden element-vs-board uncertainty, which keeps the margin slight.
